title: Selection and Paper runtime_config can still change trading behavior without mandatory version activation
description:
Expected: Any runtime choice that can affect selected stocks, target positions, order intents, fills, cash, holdings, NAV, or performance must be represented by a versioned platform runtime profile, validated execution policy activation, tail policy version, or PackageRuntimeRelease/PortfolioBindingVersion. Selection Center, Paper v2, and MiniQMT must persist the exact version/hash used for every run and should reject unversioned raw runtime_config behavior changes outside explicitly diagnostic/read-only preview paths.
Actual: Selection Center still accepts arbitrary runtime_config in run_packages and normalizes it directly when st_pit_authoritative is not enabled. PaperTradingV2PortfolioService.resolve_runtime_config_for_date still accepts runtime_config directly and normalizes it when no active runtime profile activation exists. Legacy top-level keys such as top_k, exclude_suspended, enable_sector_hmm, hmm_model_version_id, and risk_policy can alter selection/runtime behavior without a mandatory profile version or activation. Runtime variants are package-scoped and only partially wired, which further blurs the boundary.
required_verification: Production-like Selection/Paper/MiniQMT execution paths reject unversioned runtime_config keys that change trading behavior.
Versioned runtime profile activation records are persisted and copied into every selection/paper run context.
Preview/diagnostic flows, if any, are explicitly marked non-trading and cannot submit orders or mutate durable ledgers.
closure_requirements: Runtime behavior changes require profile/policy/release version references and hashes.
Legacy top-level runtime keys cannot silently bypass activation in trading execution paths.
